I don't have anything on Telltale. The knowledge I have covers only Toil & Trouble, so I can't say how Telltale wants expert reports reviewed or when it will discuss settlement. Client preferences also vary, and another client's confidential arrangements shouldn't be used as a template without checking. For Toil & Trouble, the stored instructions say the following.

**Experts**
- No testifying expert may be engaged until the client signs off. Franklin Oyelaran, the General Counsel, should get names and credentials, ideally several candidates per discipline, before we retain anyone.
- Nothing is stored about how Toil & Trouble wants expert reports reviewed, such as draft review, comment windows, or who signs off. We should ask Mr. Oyelaran.
- Rennick Odell, the product safety lead, is the technical contact, but any access to him goes through Mr. Oyelaran. We should not contact him or other employees directly.

**Settlement**
- The firm has no settlement authority. Our job is to give an assessment and a recommended range, which the client takes to its claims group.
- No offer or signal in any form goes out without Mr. Oyelaran's written approval.
- Because approvals take time, we should raise the range early and allow lead time.
- Delphine Moorcroft is copied on communications touching exposure or coverage, since she coordinates with the insurer's adjuster.
- Nothing stored sets a date for a settlement discussion. The trigger is our recommended range, and an expert result or inspection finding that changes exposure would be a natural point to give one.

**Reporting around both**
- Mr. Oyelaran wants a single-page report each month. It shows the exposure range in dollars, a few lines of status, upcoming dates, and any client decision needed. It has no narrative memo.
- We also send a page after any event that changes the range, such as an inspection result, an expert finding, or a ruling.
- Expert selection and any settlement-range recommendation should show up as decisions needed on that page.

**Staffing and budget**
- Staffing is limited to one associate and one partner, with no more than two lawyers at any deposition or hearing.
- The client wants an estimate for each phase of the matter, including expert work.

I suggest we send Mr. Oyelaran, copying Ms. Moorcroft, a short note proposing a process for expert report review and for timing the settlement-range discussion, and ask him to confirm or adjust it. I can draft that note if you'd like.
